title: Magnus Carlsen forfeits his Fast classic game against Bibisara Assaubayeva

 Himank Ghosh November 17, 2026 · 4 min read Comment Share Never miss a story
 Get our news on WhatsApp and Google
 Regular Updates Get regular updates Prefer us on Comment Share Magnus Carlsen clinched the 17th-21st place match semifinals of the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot against Bibisara Assaubayeva by winning 3 Blitz games and 2 Rapid games, drawing only 1 Blitz game - the score was 11.5-0.5 in favor of Magnus. The match was already won before the Fast Classic game.
 Magnus' interview coming into the match against Bibisara! | Video: ChessBase India 
 Magnus checking out the other games | Photo: Maria Emelianova/Total Chess Then something happened - moments after the round had started, Magnus Carlsen came out of the playing hall. Sverre from TV2 rushed to ask Magnus what had happened - and this is what he said (Special thanks to Sverre for the translation):
"There will be no classical game as I understood, the match is over. The only consequence of not showing up is that you will lose a totally useless game. I think that if you play a World Championship and it counts for points and such, I can understand. But this is not a show tournament - if the match is done, its done. In the end, if you play games after, it shall not be rated because it's always been like that. And if they want to do things differently here... yeah. This is my decision on this topic."
 Magnus Carlsen's interview after he forfeited his game! | Video: ChessBase India After 15 minutes (the default time), Bibisara came out of the playing hall. The result of the game showed Bibisara as the winner - the final score after Day 1 of the 17th-20th place semifinals was 11.5-8.5 in favor of Magnus. The game was not FIDE rated as the game was not played.
 Bibisara waiting for Magnus at the board | Photo: Abhyudaya Ram We later interviewed the Total Chess CEO and Founder Kjell Madland, who said the following:
 Interview with Kjell regarding the Magnus incident | Video: ChessBase India Q: Can you tell us what happened today with regards to the Fast Classical game of Magnus Carlsen and him not showing up to play against Bibisara Assaubayeva?
 A: Well, he was there and discussed with the arbiter team. He had already won the day - like, the system is to win the day, and he had already enough points to win the day. So then he didn't want to play the last game, and he didn't need to do it.
 Q: Was this informed to Bibisara as well beforehand or no?
 A: No, because he could play if he wanted to play. But we of course didn't discuss this with Bibisara before - that was not necessary. Before we knew what happened, we didn't know.
 Q: From tomorrow, will there be any changes in the rules? Like if someone has already won the match, do they still have to play Fast Classical?
 A: The rules are the same for everyone. We can't do any differences between the players - it's the same for everyone. So if that happens tomorrow with someone else, it happened.
We also interviewed the Chief Arbiter of the tournament, IA Anastasia Sorokina:
 Interview with the Chief Arbiter regarding the Magnus incident | Video: ChessBase India Q: I'm joined here by the chief arbiter, Anastasia Sorokina. Anastasia, this incident happened today - Magnus Carlsen didn't come to play his Fast Classic game against Bibisara. Can you tell us what happened before the game and afterwards?
 A: Yes. As you know, the result was minus-plus because Magnus didn't appear for the game. And of course, this is the result that the arbiter should apply for anyone who didn't appear for the game. Magnus came before the game, since he had already won his match by any positive or negative result of the classical game. He asked, does it influence anything - what could be in such a case? And of course, the game is not rated. So from our perspective as arbiters, there are no extra penalties for this, except the game is minus-plus, of course.
 Q: And was Bibisara informed of this discussion with Magnus, or how was it?
 A: No, because according to the regulations, we have 15 minutes default time. So since the player could change his mind, of course we started the clock. We were waiting 15 minutes, and then, as I said, the result appeared: minus-plus.
 Q: Just one final question. Was there any clause or something in the regulations which mentioned that the player has to pay a fine or something if they don't play?
 A: There is a point about the possible fees that organizers could apply, but it's not directly connected to the game. So it depends on the situation - organizers will decide.
This was the official statement given by the organizers of the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot by Founder and CEO Kjell Madland:
“The Budapest pilot is an important learning exercise for Total Chess. While we have developed the format and regulations with considerable thought and input, the real test is how they work in a live competitive environment. We want to hear directly from the players and arbiters, understand their experiences and take on board constructive feedback. Our objective is to assess whether any refinements are required before the inaugural edition in March 2027. We are not approaching this with a predetermined view that the rules need to change; rather, we want to ensure that we have tested the format thoroughly and are taking the best possible version of it into its inaugural season.”
